extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers seeking a biographical overview of comedian Doug Stanhope and his career
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography summarizing Doug Stanhope's comedic style, subjects, influences, career milestones, controversies, and media output — useful as a compact reference for understanding his approach to stand-up and public persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Black comedy; blue comedy; political satire; insult comedy; character comedy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These genre labels (from the page's infobox) indicate the stylistic categories Stanhope's work is associated with and can be used to classify or compare his material with other comedians in the same subgenres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects of material
rubrics_metrics.description: American culture; American politics; current events; recreational drug use; human sexuality; religion; family
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed subjects identify recurring thematic territory for Stanhope's jokes and indicate the topical scope a performer emulating him might cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic descriptor: profane and confrontational
rubrics_metrics.description: “His stand-up material consist of profane and confrontational observations of life.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit characterization sets an expectation for tone (profane, confrontational) and approach (observational material delivered aggressively); useful as a stylistic standard or target when evaluating or attempting similar comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Among his early comedy influences were Monty Python and National Lampoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing influences suggests aesthetic lineage (surreal/absurdism, satirical or boundary-pushing sketch humor) and can inform expectations about structure, pacing, or comedic sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocative/offensive content risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Provocative remarks have led to criticism, protests, cancellations and even violence (examples: criticism and protests after comments about the September 11 attacks; cancellation of Fringe appearances after jokes about Irish men and pedophilia; a violent affray at a show).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents concrete consequences of offensive material — an anti-pattern warning: boundary-pushing material can yield backlash, canceled bookings, hostile audiences, or safety issues; performers and bookers should weigh potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publicity stunts and unconventional pricing/offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include offering 'A Day with Doug' for £7,349 and announcing a humorous presidential run on the Libertarian ticket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual offers, stunts or satirical political gestures can generate press and audience interest; such tactics function as marketing/publicity devices though they may be polarizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markers of professional success
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning competitions and awards (San Francisco International Comedy Competition, Strathmore Press Award), being placed in critics' lists (The Guardian's '20 Best Live Shows'), and charting on Comedy Albums/Heatseekers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography treats competitions, festival awards, critical lists, and chart positions as measurable career achievements and legitimating signals for a comedian's standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded output and media formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing comedy albums, DVDs, digital specials and bootlegs; filming comedy specials and international tours/residencies (e.g., Leicester Square Theatre 25-night residency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented outputs indicate the standard portfolio for a successful stand-up career: multiple recorded specials/albums, touring, festival residencies, and multimedia releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversifying media presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearing on TV shows (Invasion of the Hidden Cameras, The Man Show, Louie), hosting radio shows and podcasts (The Doug Stanhope Podcast, SIRIUS), acting in films, and collaborating with labels/managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad media engagement — television, radio, podcasting, film, label partnerships and management deals — is presented as a path for career growth and audience expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective/touring troupe formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a group of touring comics known as The Unbookables and releasing group material (The Unbookables' Morbid Obscenity CD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forming a collective/brand with like-minded performers can create touring opportunities, shared releases, and an alternative promotional ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage persona and personal branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Noted traits include heavy alcohol consumption, thrift-store clothing, and a reputation for being 'defiantly' outspoken; these personal attributes factor into his public image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal habits and wardrobe choices contribute to a comedian's recognizable persona and can be deliberately cultivated as part of branding; they can also influence public perception and press coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of political activism with comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public endorsements and activism (endorsement of the Free State Project, support for civil unions, fundraising for an atheist tornado victim) are interwoven with his public profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using public platform for political positions and activism is presented as a component of Stanhope's career and identity; such actions can impact audience relationships and media narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and reputational risk from public statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented legal challenge: Amber Heard sued Stanhope for a 'defamatory' claim (later dropped).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public allegations or defamatory statements can trigger lawsuits and reputational consequences; performers should be aware of legal exposure when making claims about identifiable individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception as an evaluative metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Press reviews (5-star reviews mentioned) and inclusion in critics' lists are used on the page to evaluate the quality of live shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical acclaim and press coverage function on this page as external validation of performance quality and influence booking and reputation.
